# Lean

## Tools

- **`lake lint`**: Lake's lint subcommand. Runs the linter named by the `lintDriver` field of `lakefile.toml` (or the `package` block of `lakefile.lean`).
- **`batteries/runLinter`**: The Mathlib-community linter driver, supplied by the Batteries dependency. Runs the same linters Mathlib runs in CI (`unusedArguments`, `unusedHypotheses`, `docBlame`, etc.).

There is no external linter to install: `lake` ships with the Lean toolchain, and `batteries/runLinter` ships as part of the Batteries dependency that every Mathlib-downstream project already pulls in transitively. The setup work is wiring, not installation.

## Install

Do **not** install `lean` or `elan` from this skill. The bootstrap script (`bin/bootstrap-worktree`, generated by the `scaffold-lean-library` skill) handles toolchain provisioning via `elan` and `lake exe cache get`.

If a project lacks a bootstrap script, recommend running the `scaffold-lean-library` skill rather than installing `elan` ad-hoc.

## Config

### `lakefile.toml`

Confirm `lakefile.toml` declares the lint driver:

```toml
lintDriver = "batteries/runLinter"
```

Without this line, `lake lint` is a no-op. With it, `lake lint` becomes a real pre-commit gate that catches the same issues Mathlib reviewers would flag.

If the project uses `lakefile.lean` instead of `lakefile.toml`, the equivalent goes in the `package` block:

```lean
package "MyProject" where
  lintDriver := "batteries/runLinter"
```

If neither form sets `lintDriver`, offer to add it.

### Cross-language tools

Lean projects are typically paper-backed or documentation-heavy, so layer the standard cross-language stack on top:

- `markdownlint-cli2` for `*.md` files
- `cspell` for spelling
- `.editorconfig` for whitespace and encoding

If the project has `references/papers/` or `references/transcriptions/`, or if the user requests `--pandoc-academic`, use the Pandoc-academic preset rather than the generic Markdown defaults. The preset ships coordinated markdownlint and cspell configs for Pandoc citations, LaTeX math, raw `{=latex}` blocks, dense tables, YAML frontmatter titles, and transcription trees treated as excluded reference material.

## Makefile Targets

Add a `lean-lint` target gated by the `_check-mathlib-cache` private target so it fails loudly when Mathlib's prebuilt artifacts are missing rather than silently spending an hour recompiling Mathlib:

```makefile
lean-lint: _check-mathlib-cache ## Run Lean linter (batteries)
	lake lint
```

The `_check-mathlib-cache` target is part of the standard Mathlib-downstream Makefile. See `plugins/write-lean-code/skills/write-lean-code/references/comprehensive/build-infrastructure.md` for the full target set, including how `lean-lint` slots into the meta `check` target alongside `lint-markdown`, `lint-spelling`, `build`, and `test`.

If the project has a `Makefile` but no `lean-lint` target, offer to add it. If the project has no `Makefile` at all, defer to the `scaffold-lean-library` skill rather than synthesizing one here.

## CI Integration

The standard Lean CI step uses `leanprover/lean-action`, which runs `lake build` and `lake test` and (depending on inputs) `lake lint` in a single composite action:

```yaml
- uses: leanprover/lean-action@<sha> # <tag>
  with:
    test: true
    lint: true
```

If `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already uses `leanprover/lean-action`, confirm the `lint: true` input is set; if not, recommend adding it (or recommend a dedicated `lake lint` step if the project deliberately splits build, test, and lint into separate jobs).

If no Lean CI workflow exists, defer to the `scaffold-lean-library` skill rather than synthesizing one here.

## Notes

- `lake lint` only works after Mathlib's prebuilt artifacts have been fetched (`lake exe cache get`). Run `make bootstrap` (or `bin/bootstrap-worktree`) once per fresh clone or worktree before the first `make lean-lint`.
- The `lean-lint` target is intentionally separate from the meta `lint` target (`lint: lint-markdown lint-spelling`). `lean-lint` is gated on Mathlib cache presence; `lint-markdown` and `lint-spelling` are not. Combining them would couple the cheap text linters to the expensive Lean cache check.
- For the test-library mirroring discipline that complements `lake lint` (compile-time `example`-based API regression tests under `<Name>Test/`), see the `write-lean-tests` skill.
